regimes.description: Orderly rising market with shallow pauses and positive drift.
regimes.name: Trend Up
risk_notes: Leveraged long products may compound favorably, but late pullbacks can erase gains quickly.
Inverse products can lose value steadily even without a single large up day.
use_cases: Testing positive compounding in a persistent advance.
Comparing stop and take-profit bands after a favorable start.

regimes.description: Persistent selloff with brief relief rallies that fail.
regimes.name: Trend Down
risk_notes: Long leveraged products can compound losses faster than a simple multiple suggests.
Brief relief rallies can materially hurt inverse daily reset exposure sizing.
use_cases: Stress testing long leveraged drawdown paths.
Reviewing inverse product behavior during failed bounces.

regimes.description: Alternating up and down sessions with limited net direction.
regimes.name: Chop
risk_notes: Alternating returns can create path decay even when the underlying ends near flat.
Stop and take-profit bands may trigger repeatedly in both directions.
use_cases: Demonstrating volatility decay from daily reset leverage.
Comparing trend assumptions against sideways whipsaw conditions.

regimes.description: Large downside gap followed by unstable trading and a partial attempt to stabilize.
regimes.name: Gap Down
risk_notes: Gap moves can bypass planning bands and create modeled losses before any exit is possible.
Single-name event risk can dominate management-fee or ordinary volatility assumptions.
use_cases: Single-stock earnings or regulatory event stress tests.
Checking whether a loss budget survives a discontinuous first move.

regimes.description: Initial drawdown followed by stabilization and a sharp recovery attempt.
regimes.name: Rebound
risk_notes: Losses early in the path reduce the NAV base that participates in a later rebound.
Inverse products can give back gains quickly if the recovery accelerates.
use_cases: Testing whether a leveraged position can recover after an early stop zone.
Reviewing inverse hedge exit rules after an initial selloff.

regimes.description: Sequence of large moves in both directions, modeling clustered high volatility.
regimes.name: Volatility Cluster
risk_notes: Large alternating moves can produce material decay even if the final underlying move is modest.
Modeled NAV can become highly sensitive to the order of daily returns.
use_cases: Stress testing path dependence during high-volatility regimes.
Comparing risk bands under clustered large-move conditions.
